summary: Delivered the POST local infrastructure stack as a Docker Compose project: PostgreSQL 16 + pgvector 0.8.6 (pgvector/pgvector:0.8.6-pg16), Redis 7.4.11-alpine, MinIO RELEASE.2025-09-07T16-13-09Z (quay.io — MinIO no longer publishes to Docker Hub), Gitea 1.27.3, Mailpit v1.31.1. All exact tags, healthchecks with real readiness probes on every service, named volumes, all host ports bound to 127.0.0.1 only, overridable ports/credentials via environment variables (no root .env created, no COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME hardcoded). One-command idempotent init (make infra-init) creates the MinIO bucket 'post' and the Gitea admin 'postadmin', test org 'post-test', and service account 'post-git-svc' — re-runs are pure no-ops (verified twice back-to-back plus once after a down/up cycle). Gitea's dev mailer is wired to Mailpit (nothing leaves the host). Applications remain host-native. Makefile targets (infra-up/infra-init/infra/infra-down/infra-ps/infra-logs) documented in make help; ops/DEV_COMMANDS.md updated; full dev guide in infra/docker/README.md. All G1 tests executed with real output: all-healthy compose ps, idempotency, pgvector enable-ability, down/up persistence, ./ops/doctor.sh still exit 0. Note: Gitea >= 1.27 removed native 'service accounts' — the service account is modeled as a token-only bot user plus an org team (the supported machine-identity mechanism in 1.27); flagged for Supervisor confirmation in risks.

No .env/.env.example created at repo root (T0004's scope untouched). Defaults are inline ${VAR:-default} in docker-compose.yml, exactly as the requirement allows.

docker-compose.yml sets no name: — the project ran under rddev's preset posttask-t0003. All 8 host ports are ${VAR:-default} variables (override table in README); the README shows a full second-isolated-stack example.

Compose comments and README state ADR-019: internal Git provider, UI for debugging only, nothing presents it as product surface. Registration disabled (GITEA__service__DISABLE_REGISTRATION=true), offline mode on, dev mail to Mailpit only.
ops/DEV_COMMANDS.md: new 本地基础设施 section with all make infra commands, ports, credentials summary, isolation and pin notes, pointing to infra/docker/README.md for the full table.

acceptance.criterion: Stack wired into the Makefile as documented targets (requirement 10)
acceptance.evidence: infra-up, infra-init, infra, infra-down, infra-ps, infra-logs added to .PHONY with ## help lines; all appear in make help; all exercised successfully during G1.

acceptance.criterion: Applications remain host-native; this task delivers infrastructure only (task-package requirement)
acceptance.evidence: The compose file defines only the five infrastructure services; no Go API, worker, MCP server, rddev, Next.js or Python adapter image is built or run anywhere in the diff.

risks: Gitea >= 1.27 removed native 'service accounts' (verified: 1.27.3 swagger has no service_accounts endpoints, no ServiceAccount types, no membership endpoints). The task's 'Gitea service account' is delivered as a token-only bot user (post-git-svc, gitea admin user create --user-type bot) plus an org team 'svc' with write permission (Gitea 1.27 routes org membership through teams). This is a judgment call for Supervisor confirmation; downgrading to gitea/gitea:1.26.4 (which still has native service accounts) is a one-line change if literal service accounts are preferred.

MinIO no longer publishes to Docker Hub (pull denied: 'requested access to the resource is denied'; Hub API 404 for the minio namespace). The pinned official registry is quay.io/minio/minio:RELEASE.2025-09-07T16-13-09Z.

Product specs do not pin bucket/org/account names: I chose bucket 'post', org 'post-test', service account 'post-git-svc', admin 'postadmin' (all clearly dev-flavored, overridable via env vars). L1 judgment call — confirm or rename with Supervisor before T0004+ consumes them.

The pinned MinIO release has a newer hotfix variant tag (RELEASE.2025-09-07T16-13-09Z.hotfix.7aa24e772) on quay.io; I pinned the plain RELEASE tag (canonical release identifier). Bump decision left to Supervisor.

Admin/service-account passwords and the bot access token are initial-only: they are set at first creation and printed once (token). Re-runs are no-ops by design, so later env overrides of the password do not retroactively apply. Admins can mint new bot tokens via 'gitea admin user generate-access-token'. Documented in the README.

Gitea logs a warning on boot ('connecting over insecure SMTP protocol to non-local address is not recommended'): expected — dev mail goes to Mailpit in plain SMTP on purpose; documented in README troubleshooting.
Mailpit messages are ephemeral by design (in-memory, no volume) — documented; not product state.
Worker-guard false positive: a read-only grep command containing the words 'service'/'system' was blocked as 'package/system service mutation'. Reported as a constraint; no retry attempted.

Leftover host cruft from testing: one stopped scratch container 'mc-ready-test' (a minio probe used to verify mc behavior) remains on the Docker host; 'docker rm' is blocked for Workers, so the Supervisor/operator may remove it. Also the test volumes posttask-t0003_* were intentionally kept (persistence evidence) with the stack down.

initdb bootstrap (01-init.sh) and init scripts interpolate dev credentials into SQL/shell; they are dev-only values and the scripts run once per volume lifetime or are existence-checked, but quoting assumes no exotic characters in overridden values.
follow_up_issues: GitProvider adapter tasks should consume the post-git-svc bot/token flow for Gitea API access (token printed on first init run; 'gitea admin user generate-access-token' mints more).
Consider bumping the MinIO pin to the hotfix variant tag or the next RELEASE when image pins are next reviewed.
T0009 (rddev env up / env reset) should delegate to these compose targets rather than reimplementing them; rddev doctor remains the canonical preflight.
If Supervisor prefers native Gitea service accounts, downgrade the gitea pin to 1.26.4 and simplify the init script (direct service_accounts endpoints).
